steps.what: 0. steps.what: 4. guards.what: G6 — `RunManager.ShouldApplyTutorialModifications()` (RunManager.cs:698-717) gates `ActModel.ApplyDiscoveryOrderModifications(UnlockState)` (step 3), which overrides an act's rolled boss (and, per-act, other encounters via the abstract `ApplyActDiscoveryOrderModifications`) to the first one in `BossDiscoveryOrder` the profile's `UnlockState.HasSeenEncounter` has NOT yet seen
guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `ActModel.ApplyDiscoveryOrderModifications` is ported as `RoomSet.apply_discovery_order_modifications`, run after every act's generation exactly where RunManager.cs:678-684 runs it (and drawing no RNG, so no stream shifts): the boss override walks each act's transcribed `BossDiscoveryOrder`, and Overgrowth's `ApplyActDiscoveryOrderModifications` first-run lineup is ported with `RoomSet.SwapToOrCreateAtIndex`'s two arms. It reads a new `rooms.UnlockState` (HasSeenEncounter + NumberOfRuns) that `RunState` takes as a parameter. The DEFAULT is `UnlockState.VETERAN` (has seen everything), which makes the pass a no-op — and the record's premise that no fixture carries discovery history is REFUTED: both installed Ironclad captures store `players[0].unlock_state` with number_of_runs=999999999 and all 12 bosses seen, so the conformance runner now feeds the recording's OWN profile and the no-op is a measured fact rather than an assumption. `rooms.py`'s line comment calling this a tutorial-only path (the bug class this guard filed) is rewritten. Tests: test/test_discovery_order.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: The method's own name and the sim's comment describing it ('tutorial mods are off for real runs — see the module docstring', rooms.py:94-95) both suggest this is a first-run-only onboarding path. Read against the CODE (not the name or the comment, per bug class 1/30): `ShouldApplyTutorialModifications` returns `true` for ANY run where `!ForceDiscoveryOrderModifications`, `TestMode.IsOff`, and `State.GameMode == Standard` — i.e. it is the DEFAULT for every ordinary, non-test, Standard-mode game (single- or multiplayer; no player-count check exists in the method body despite its own XML summary claiming one), not a tutorial-only exception. `rooms.py`'s module-level docstring DOES separately, honestly disclose this as a known omission ('Deviations from the source... no boss discovery-order override'), so this is not a hidden or misrepresented gap — but the INDIVIDUAL comment at rooms.py:94-95 mischaracterizes WHY it is safe to skip, which risks the omission being re-justified on a false premise the next time someone reads it. LIVE because it requires no ascension, no multiplayer, and no test-mode opt-out — it is the boss-selection path EVERY real single-player Ironclad conformance run actually takes, and its outcome (which boss a profile with unseen bosses fights) depends on `UnlockState.HasSeenEncounter`, a PROFILE-scoped discovery history the sim never models at all (see G10). Executed: `py audit/tools/run_layer_probes.py discovery-order` confirms (a) the C# guard chain has no player-count or first-run check, (b) `ApplyDiscoveryOrderModifications`/`ApplyActDiscoveryOrderModifications`/`BossDiscoveryOrder`/`HasSeenEncounter` have zero references anywhere under `sts2_rl/`. Whether any specific conformance seed's recorded boss fight actually diverges from a fresh `RoomSet` roll depends on that PLAYER's own discovery history at the time of the recording, which this seam cannot determine (no save/profile fixture carries it) — filed as live because the MECHANISM is unconditionally reachable in scope, not because a specific seed's divergence was reproduced. `BossDiscoveryOrder`/`ApplyActDiscoveryOrderModifications`'s own per-act CONTENT is `rooms_and_map`'s file (`ActModel.cs`, cited here in extra_sources only for the call chain); this entry is filed under run_layer because the GATE (`ShouldApplyTutorialModifications`) and its CALL SITE live in `RunManager.cs`, this seam's own file. Proposed mechanism id: `run_layer/discovery_order`.

guards.issue: A pure ordering swap with no value divergence today. Executed: `py audit/tools/run_layer_probes.py starting-relic-order` confirms `BurningBlood.cs` (Ironclad's only starting relic, and the only starting relic reachable in this Ironclad-only sim) has no `AfterObtained` override anywhere in its body (`grep -n AfterObtained src/Core/Models/Relics/BurningBlood.cs` returns zero matches; its one override is `AfterCombatVictory`, an in-combat hook unrelated to this ordering).
